211:       timeout = 100000;
212:       while ((sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO) & BK7258_SDIO_TX_READY) == 0)
213:         {
214:           if (timeout == 0)
215:             {
216:               return -ETIMEDOUT;
217:             }
218: 
219:           timeout--;
220:           up_udelay(1);
221:         }
222: 
223:       memcpy(&word, priv->tx_buffer, copy);
224:       sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_TX_FIFO, word);
225:       priv->tx_buffer += copy;
226:       priv->remaining -= copy;
227:     }
228: 
229:   return OK;
230: }

232: static int sdio_interrupt(int irq, FAR void *context, FAR void *arg)
233: {
234:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = &g_sdio;
235:   uint32_t status;
236:   uint32_t clear;
237: 
238:   (void)irq;
239:   (void)context;
240:   (void)arg;
241: 
242:   status = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS);
243:   clear = status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
244:                      BK7258_SDIO_DATA_WRITE_END |
245:                      BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
246:                      BK7258_SDIO_RX_NEED_READ |
247:                      BK7258_SDIO_TX_NEED_WRITE |
248:                      BK7258_SDIO_TX_FIFO_EMPTY |
249:                      BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_OK |
250:                      BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_FAIL);
251: 
252:   if (priv->data_active &&
253:       (status & ((priv->data_write ? BK7258_SDIO_DATA_WRITE_END :
254:                                     BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END) |
255:                   BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT)) != 0)
256:     {
257:       bool write_accepted = true;
258: 
259:       if (priv->data_write &&
260:           (status & BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT) == 0)
261:         {
262:           write_accepted = sdio_write_accepted(&status);
263:           clear = status & (BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
264:                             BK7258_SDIO_DATA_WRITE_END |
265:                             BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
266:                             BK7258_SDIO_RX_NEED_READ |
267:                             BK7258_SDIO_TX_NEED_WRITE |
268:                             BK7258_SDIO_TX_FIFO_EMPTY |
269:                             BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_OK |
270:                             BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_FAIL);
271:         }
272: 
273:       priv->irq_status = status;
274:       if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT) != 0)
275:         {
276:           priv->data_result = -ETIMEDOUT;
277:         }
278:       else if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_FAIL) != 0 ||
279:                (!priv->data_write &&
280:                 (status & BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CRC_OK) == 0))
281:         {
282:           priv->data_result = -EIO;
283:         }
284:       else if (priv->data_write &&
285:                (priv->remaining != 0 || !write_accepted))
286:         {
287:           priv->data_result = -EIO;
288:         }
289:       else
290:         {
291:           priv->data_result = OK;
292:         }
293: 
294:       priv->data_active = false;
295:       if (clear != 0)
296:         {
297:           sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS, clear);
298:         }
299: 
300:       nxsem_post(&priv->data_sem);
301:     }
302:   else if (clear != 0)
303:     {
304:       sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS, clear);
305:     }
306: 
307:   return OK;
308: }

310: static int sdio_wait_command(struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv, uint32_t cmd)
311: {
312:   clock_t deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(1000);
313:   uint32_t status;
314: 
315:   for (;;)
316:     {
317:       status = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS);
318:       if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
319:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
320:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT)) != 0)
321:         {
322:           break;
323:         }
324: 
325:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
326:         {
327:           printf("SDIO CMD%u timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
328:                  (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
329:                  (unsigned long)status);
330:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
331:         }
332: 
333:       /* At transfer speed the RX FIFO can fill before a 100 us sleep
334:        * expires.  Keep the PIO loop tight while data is active; otherwise a
335:        * 512-byte sector consistently overflows after the first 256 bytes. */
336:       if (!priv->data_active)
337:         {
338:           nxsig_usleep(100);
339:         }
340:     }
341: 
342:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
343:              status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
344:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
345:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT |
346:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_OK |
347:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL));
348: 
349:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT) != 0)
350:     {
351:       printf("SDIO CMD%u response timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
352:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
353:              (unsigned long)status);
354:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
355:     }
356: 
357:   /* The BK7258 host reports CRC failure for the open-drain/long-response
358:    * identification commands even when the vendor stack accepts the response.
359:    * Armino explicitly tolerates this for ACMD41, CMD2 and CMD9.  Keep the
360:    * same compatibility rule while preserving CRC errors for normal R1/R7.
361:    */
362:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL) != 0 &&
363:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != SD_ACMDIDX41 &&
364:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX2 &&
365:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9)
366:     {
367:       printf("SDIO CMD%u CRC error status=0x%08lx\n",
368:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
369:              (unsigned long)status);
370:       return -EIO;
371:     }
372: 
373:   return OK;
374: }

376: static int sdio_sendcmd(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev, uint32_t cmd,
377:                          uint32_t arg)
378: {
379:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
380:   uint32_t response;
381:   uint32_t value;
382: 
383:   response = (cmd & MMCSD_RESPONSE_MASK) >> MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT;
384:   value = ((cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) << BK7258_SDIO_CMD_INDEX_SHIFT);
385:   if (response != MMCSD_NO_RESPONSE)
386:     {
387:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE;
388:     }
389:   if (response == (MMCSD_R2_RESPONSE >> MMCSD_RESPONSE_SHIFT))
390:     {
391:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CMD_LONG;
392:     }
393:   if (response != MMCSD_NO_RESPONSE &&
394:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX2 &&
395:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9 &&
396:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != SD_ACMDIDX41)
397:     {
398:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_CHECK;
399:     }
400: 
401:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_CMD_ARGUMENT, arg);
402:   priv->last_cmd = cmd;
403:   priv->last_cmd_result = -EINPROGRESS;
404:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CTRL, value | BK7258_SDIO_CMD_START);
405:   return OK;
406: }

583: static int sdio_recvsetup(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev, FAR uint8_t *buffer,
584:                           size_t nbytes)
585: {
586:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
587:   uint32_t value;
588: 
589:   if (buffer == NULL || nbytes == 0 || priv->blocklen == 0 ||
590:       priv->nblocks == 0 || nbytes != (priv->blocklen * priv->nblocks))
591:     {
592:       return -EINVAL;
593:     }
594: 
595:   /* Match the vendor read setup order: program timeout and clear stale W1C
596:    * status before asserting the RX FIFO and SD state resets. */
597:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMER, BK7258_SDIO_TIMEOUT);
598:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS, 0xffffffffu);
599:   while (nxsem_trywait(&priv->data_sem) == OK)
600:     {
601:     }
602: 
603:   /* Complete the vendor V2 reset pulse before configuring the receive
604:    * transaction. */
605:   value = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO);
606:   value &= ~(0xffffu | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
607:              BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_TX_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET);
608:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
609: 
610:   value |= 0x0101u | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
611:            BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_RECOVERY;
612:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
613: 
614:   value = ((priv->blocklen << BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_SHIFT) &
615:            BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_MASK) | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BYTE_SELECT;
616:   /* BK7258 V2 uses its multi-block data engine for 512-byte reads even when
617:    * the card command is CMD17. Short register transfers such as SCR remain
618:    * in single-block mode. */
619: 
620:   if (priv->blocklen == 512)
621:     {
622:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_DATA_MULTIBLOCK;
623:     }
624:   /* Keep configuration and start as separate writes, matching the vendor
625:    * set_read_multi_block_data()/start_receive_data() sequence. */
626:   priv->buffer = buffer;
627:   priv->remaining = nbytes;
628:   priv->irq_status = 0;
629:   priv->data_result = -EINPROGRESS;
630:   priv->data_active = true;
631:   priv->data_write = false;
632:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, value);
633:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_INT_MASK, 0,
634:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
635:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT);
636:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, value | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_ENABLE);
637: 
638:   /* The vendor card driver requires this settling interval after starting
639:    * the receive engine; without it the receive-end event can be missed. */
640: 
641:   nxsig_usleep(2000);
642:   return OK;
643: }

645: static int sdio_sendsetup(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev,
646:                            FAR const uint8_t *buffer, size_t nbytes)
647: {
648:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
649:   uint32_t value;
650:   int ret;
651: 
652:   if (buffer == NULL || nbytes != 512 || priv->blocklen != 512 ||
653:       priv->nblocks != 1)
654:     {
655:       return -EINVAL;
656:     }
657: 
658:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMER, BK7258_SDIO_TIMEOUT);
659:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS, 0xffffffffu);
660:   while (nxsem_trywait(&priv->data_sem) == OK)
661:     {
662:     }
663: 
664:   value = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO);
665:   value &= ~(0xffffu | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
666:              BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_TX_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET |
667:              BK7258_SDIO_HOST_WRITE_BLOCK);
668:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
669: 
670:   value |= 0x0101u | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_TX_RESET |
671:            BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_RECOVERY;
672:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
673: 
674:   value = ((priv->blocklen << BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_SHIFT) &
675:             BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_MASK) | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BYTE_SELECT;
676:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, value);
677: 
678:   priv->buffer = NULL;
679:   priv->tx_buffer = buffer;
680:   priv->remaining = nbytes;
681:   priv->irq_status = 0;
682:   priv->data_result = -EINPROGRESS;
683:   priv->data_active = true;
684:   priv->data_write = true;
685: 
686:   ret = sdio_fill_tx_fifo(priv);
687:   if (ret < 0)
688:     {
689:       sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, 0);
690:       modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_INT_MASK,
691:                   BK7258_SDIO_DATA_WRITE_END |
692:                   BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
693:                   BK7258_SDIO_TX_NEED_WRITE |
694:                   BK7258_SDIO_TX_FIFO_EMPTY |
695:                   BK7258_SDIO_TX_CLOCK_GATE, 0);
696:       sdio_reset_data_state();
697:       priv->data_active = false;
698:       priv->data_result = ret;
699:       priv->tx_buffer = NULL;
700:       nxsem_post(&priv->data_sem);
701:       return ret;
702:     }
703: 
704:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_INT_MASK, 0,
705:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_WRITE_END |
706:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT |
707:               BK7258_SDIO_TX_CLOCK_GATE);
708:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL,
709:              value | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_WRITE_ENABLE);
710:   return OK;
711: }

746: static int sdio_drain_fifo(FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv)
747: {
748:   while (priv->remaining != 0)
749:     {
750:       uint32_t word;
751:       unsigned int timeout = 400;
752:       size_t copy = priv->remaining < sizeof(word) ? priv->remaining :
753:                     sizeof(word);
754: 
755:       while ((sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO) & BK7258_SDIO_RX_READY) == 0)
756:         {
757:           if (timeout == 0)
758:             {
759:               return -EIO;
760:             }
761: 
762:           timeout--;
763:           up_udelay(1);
764:         }
765: 
766:       word = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_RX_FIFO);
767:       memcpy(priv->buffer, &word, copy);
768:       priv->buffer += copy;
769:       priv->remaining -= copy;
770:     }
771: 
772:   return OK;
773: }

775: static sdio_eventset_t sdio_eventwait(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev)
776: {
777:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
778:   uint32_t status;
779:   int ret;
780: 
781:   if ((priv->wait_events & SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT) != 0)
782:     {

27: 
28: enum bk7258_mmcsd_state_e
29: {
30:   BK7258_MMCSD_NOT_STARTED = 0,
31:   BK7258_MMCSD_RUNNING,
32:   BK7258_MMCSD_COMPLETE
33: };

35: static mutex_t g_mmcsd_lock = NXMUTEX_INITIALIZER;

44: static bool bk7258_block_exists(FAR const char *path)
45: {
46:   FAR struct inode *inode;
47:   int ret;
48: 
49:   ret = open_blockdriver(path, 0, &inode);
50:   if (ret < 0)
51:     {
52:       return false;
53:     }
54: 
55:   close_blockdriver(inode);
56:   return true;
57: }

59: static int bk7258_mmcsd_mount_locked(FAR const char *source)
60: {
61: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_SDNAND_AUTOMOUNT
62:   FAR const char *mount_source = source;
63:   int ret;
64: 
65:   if (g_mmcsd_maintenance)
66:     {
67:       return -EBUSY;
68:     }
69: 
70:   if (g_mmcsd_mounted)
71:     {
72:       if (source == NULL || strcmp(source, g_mount_source) == 0)
73:         {
74:           return OK;
75:         }
76: 
77:       return -EBUSY;
78:     }
79: 
80:   if (mount_source == NULL)
81:     {
82:       mount_source = g_partition_result == OK &&
83:                      bk7258_block_exists("/dev/mmcsd0p0") ?
84:                      "/dev/mmcsd0p0" : "/dev/mmcsd0";
85:     }
86: 
87:   if (!bk7258_block_exists(mount_source))
88:     {
89:       return -ENOENT;
90:     }
91: 
92:   if (mkdir("/mnt", 0777) < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
93:     {
94:       return -errno;
95:     }
96: 
97:   if (mkdir(CONFIG_BK7258_SDNAND_MOUNTPOINT, 0777) < 0 && errno != EEXIST)
98:     {
99:       return -errno;
100:     }
101: 
102:   ret = nx_mount(mount_source, CONFIG_BK7258_SDNAND_MOUNTPOINT,
103:                  "vfat", 0, NULL);
104:   if (ret < 0)
105:     {
106:       printf("SD-NAND VFAT mount failed: source=%s target=%s error=%d\n",
107:              mount_source, CONFIG_BK7258_SDNAND_MOUNTPOINT, ret);
108:       return ret;
109:     }
110: 
111:   strlcpy(g_mount_source, mount_source, sizeof(g_mount_source));
112:   g_mmcsd_mounted = true;
113:   printf("SD-NAND persistent VFAT mounted: %s -> %s\n",
114:          g_mount_source, CONFIG_BK7258_SDNAND_MOUNTPOINT);
115:   return OK;
116: #else
117:   (void)source;
118:   return -ENOTSUP;
119: #endif

136:   ret = register_blockpartition(path, 0, "/dev/mmcsd0",
137:                                 part->firstblock, part->nblocks);
138:   if (ret == -EEXIST && bk7258_block_exists(path))
139:     {

141:     }

156: static int bk7258_mmcsd_probe(void)
157: {
158:   FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev;
159:   FAR struct inode *inode;
160:   int ret;
161: 
162:   dev = bk7258_sdio_initialize(0);
163:   if (dev == NULL)
164:     {
165:       printf("SDIO initialize failed\n");
166:       return -ENODEV;
167:     }
168: 
169:   ret = mmcsd_slotinitialize(0, dev);
170:   if (ret < 0)
171:     {
172:       printf("MMCSD registration/probe failed, error=%d\n", ret);
173:       return ret;
174:     }
175: 
176:   ret = open_blockdriver("/dev/mmcsd0", MS_RDONLY, &inode);
177:   if (ret == -ENOENT)
178:     {
179:       unsigned int elapsed;
180: 
181:       for (elapsed = 0; elapsed < BK7258_MMCSD_PROBE_WAIT_MS;
182:            elapsed += BK7258_MMCSD_PROBE_POLL_US / 1000)
183:         {
184:           nxsig_usleep(BK7258_MMCSD_PROBE_POLL_US);
185:           ret = open_blockdriver("/dev/mmcsd0", MS_RDONLY, &inode);
186:           if (ret != -ENOENT)
187:             {
188:               break;
189:             }
190:         }
191:     }
192: 
193:   if (ret < 0)
194:     {
195:       printf("MMCSD probe did not register /dev/mmcsd0, error=%d\n", ret);
196:       return ret;
197:     }
198: 
199:   close_blockdriver(inode);
200: 
201:   printf("SD-NAND MMCSD ready: /dev/mmcsd0\n");
202: 
203: #ifdef CONFIG_MBR_PARTITION
204:   g_partition_result = -ENOENT;
205:   ret = parse_block_partition("/dev/mmcsd0", bk7258_partition_handler, NULL);
206:   if (ret < 0)
207:     {
208:       printf("SD-NAND has no parseable MBR, using super-floppy path: %d\n",
209:              ret);
210:     }
211: #endif
212: 
213: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_SDNAND_AUTOMOUNT
214:   ret = bk7258_mmcsd_mount_locked(NULL);
215:   if (ret < 0)
216:     {
217:       printf("SD-NAND initialized without persistent mount, error=%d\n",
218:              ret);
219:     }
220: #endif
221: 
222:   return OK;
223: }

225: int bk7258_mmcsd_initialize(void)
226: {
227:   FAR struct inode *inode;
228:   int ret;
229: 
230:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
231:   if (ret < 0)
232:     {
233:       return ret;
234:     }
235: 
236:   if (g_mmcsd_state == BK7258_MMCSD_COMPLETE)
237:     {
238:       ret = open_blockdriver("/dev/mmcsd0", MS_RDONLY, &inode);
239:       if (ret == OK)
240:         {
241:           close_blockdriver(inode);
242: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_SDNAND_AUTOMOUNT
243:           if (!g_mmcsd_mounted)
244:             {
245:               ret = bk7258_mmcsd_mount_locked(NULL);
246:             }
247: #endif
248:         }
249:       else
250:         {
251:           ret = g_mmcsd_result;
252:         }
253: 
254:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
255:       return ret;
256:     }
257: 
258:   g_mmcsd_state = BK7258_MMCSD_RUNNING;
259:   ret = bk7258_mmcsd_probe();
260:   g_mmcsd_result = ret;
261:   g_mmcsd_state = BK7258_MMCSD_COMPLETE;
262:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
263:   return ret;
264: }

272:     {
273:       return ret;
274:     }
275: 
276:   if (g_mmcsd_state != BK7258_MMCSD_COMPLETE ||
277:       !bk7258_block_exists("/dev/mmcsd0"))
278:     {
279:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
280:       return -ENODEV;
281:     }
282: 
283:   ret = bk7258_mmcsd_mount_locked(source);
284:   if (ret == OK)
285:     {
286:       g_mmcsd_result = OK;
287:     }
288: 
289:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
290:   return ret;
291: }

293: int bk7258_mmcsd_maintenance_begin(void)
294: {
295:   int ret;
296: 
297:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
298:   if (ret < 0)
299:     {
300:       return ret;
301:     }
302: 
303:   if (g_mmcsd_state != BK7258_MMCSD_COMPLETE ||
304:       !bk7258_block_exists("/dev/mmcsd0"))
305:     {
306:       ret = -ENODEV;
307:       goto out_unlock;
308:     }
309: 
310:   if (g_mmcsd_maintenance)
311:     {
312:       ret = -EBUSY;
313:       goto out_unlock;
314:     }
315: 
316:   g_mmcsd_maintenance = true;
317:   if (g_mmcsd_mounted)
318:     {
319:       ret = nx_umount2(CONFIG_BK7258_SDNAND_MOUNTPOINT, 0);
320:       if (ret < 0)
321:         {
322:           g_mmcsd_maintenance = false;
323:           goto out_unlock;
324:         }
325: 
326:       g_mmcsd_mounted = false;
327:       g_mount_source[0] = '\0';
328:     }
329: 
330:   ret = OK;
331: 
332: out_unlock:
333:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
334:   return ret;
335: }

337: void bk7258_mmcsd_maintenance_abort(void)
338: {
339:   if (nxmutex_lock(&g_mmcsd_lock) == OK)
340:     {
341:       g_mmcsd_maintenance = false;
342:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
343:     }
344: }

346: int bk7258_mmcsd_maintenance_complete(FAR const char *source,
347:                                       bool whole_disk)
348: {
349:   char path[sizeof("/dev/mmcsd0p0")];
350:   unsigned int index;
351:   int ret;
352: 
353:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
354:   if (ret < 0)
355:     {
356:       return ret;
357:     }
358: 
359:   if (!g_mmcsd_maintenance)
360:     {
361:       ret = -EINVAL;
362:       goto out_unlock;
363:     }
364: 
365:   if (whole_disk)
366:     {
367:       for (index = 0; index < 10; index++)

369:           snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/dev/mmcsd0p%u", index);
370:           if (bk7258_block_exists(path))
371:             {
372:               (void)unregister_blockdriver(path);
373:             }
374:         }
375: 
376:       g_partition_result = -ENOENT;
377:     }
378: 
379:   g_mmcsd_maintenance = false;
380:   ret = bk7258_mmcsd_mount_locked(source);
381: 
382: out_unlock:
383:   nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);
384:   return ret;
385: }

395:     }
396: 
397:   if (!g_mmcsd_mounted)
398:     {
399:       nxmutex_unlock(&g_mmcsd_lock);

401:     }
402: 
403:   ret = nx_umount2(CONFIG_BK7258_SDNAND_MOUNTPOINT, 0);
404:   if (ret == OK)
405:     {
406:       g_mmcsd_mounted = false;
407:       g_mount_source[0] = '\0';
408:     }

90: static void register_partition(FAR struct partition_s *part, FAR void *arg)
91: {
92:   if (part->name[0] != '\0')
93:     {
94:       FAR struct partition_register_s *reg = arg;
95:       FAR struct partition_state_s *state = reg->state;
96:       FAR char *path;
97: 
98:       path = lib_get_tempbuffer(PATH_MAX);
99:       if (path == NULL)
100:         {
101:           return;
102:         }
103: 
104:       snprintf(path, PATH_MAX, "%s/%s", reg->dir, part->name);
105:       if (state->blk != NULL)
106:         {
107:           register_partition_with_inode(path, 0660, state->blk,
108:                                         part->firstblock, part->nblocks);
109:         }
110: #ifdef CONFIG_MTD
111:       else
112:         {
113:           register_partition_with_mtd(path, 0660, state->mtd,
114:                                       part->firstblock, part->nblocks);
115:         }
116: #endif
117: 
118:       lib_put_tempbuffer(path);
119:     }

122: /****************************************************************************
123:  * Name: parse_partition
124:  *
125:  * Description:
126:  *   parse the partition table.
127:  *
128:  * Input Parameters:
129:  *   state   - The partition table state
130:  *   handler - The function to be called for each found partition
131:  *   arg     - A caller provided value to return with the handler
132:  *
133:  * Returned Value:
134:  *   Zero on success; A negated errno value is returned on a failure
135:  *
136:  ****************************************************************************/
137: 
138: static int parse_partition(FAR struct partition_state_s *state,
139:                            partition_handler_t handler,
140:                            FAR void *arg)
141: {
142:   int i;
143:   int ret = 0;
144:   struct partition_register_s reg =
145:   {
146:     state, arg ? arg : "/dev"
147:   };
148: 
149:   if (handler == NULL)
150:     {
151:       handler = register_partition;
152:       arg = ®
153:     }
154: 
155:   for (i = 0; g_parser[i] != NULL; i++)
156:     {
157:       ret = g_parser[i](state, handler, arg);
158:       if (ret >= 0)
159:         {
160:           break;
161:         }
162:     }
163: 
164:   return ret;
165: }

171: int read_partition_block(FAR struct partition_state_s *state,
172:                          FAR void *buffer, size_t startblock,
173:                          size_t nblocks)
174: {
175:   if (state->blk)
176:     {
177:       return state->blk->u.i_bops->read(state->blk,
178:                                         buffer, startblock, nblocks);
179:     }
180:   else
181:     {
182:       return state->mtd->bread(state->mtd, startblock, nblocks, buffer);
183:     }
184: }

186: /****************************************************************************
187:  * Name: parse_block_partition
188:  *
189:  * Description:
190:  *   parse the partition table on a block device.
191:  *
192:  * Input Parameters:
193:  *   path    - The block device to be parsed
194:  *   handler - The function to be called for each found partition
195:  *   arg     - A caller provided value to return with the handler
196:  *
197:  * Returned Value:
198:  *   Zero on success; A negated errno value is returned on a failure
199:  *
200:  ****************************************************************************/
201: 
202: int parse_block_partition(FAR const char *path,
203:                           partition_handler_t handler,
204:                           FAR void *arg)
205: {
206:   struct partition_state_s state;
207:   struct mtd_geometry_s mgeo;
208:   struct geometry geo;
209:   int ret;
210: 
211:   ret = open_blockdriver(path, MS_RDONLY, &state.blk);
212:   if (ret < 0)
213:     {
214:       return ret;
215:     }
216: 
217:   state.mtd = NULL;
218: 
219:   if (state.blk->u.i_bops->ioctl != NULL &&
220:       state.blk->u.i_bops->ioctl(state.blk, MTDIOC_GEOMETRY,
221:                                  (unsigned long)(uintptr_t)&mgeo) >= 0)
222:     {
223:       DEBUGASSERT(mgeo.blocksize);
224: 
225:       state.blocksize = mgeo.blocksize;
226:       state.erasesize = mgeo.erasesize;
227:       state.nblocks   = mgeo.neraseblocks;
228:       state.nblocks  *= mgeo.erasesize / mgeo.blocksize;
229: 
230:       ret = parse_partition(&state, handler, arg);
231:     }
232:   else
233:     {
234:       ret = state.blk->u.i_bops->geometry(state.blk, &geo);
235:       if (ret >= 0)
236:         {
237:           DEBUGASSERT(geo.geo_sectorsize);
238: 
239:           state.blocksize = geo.geo_sectorsize;
240:           state.erasesize = geo.geo_sectorsize;
241:           state.nblocks   = geo.geo_nsectors;
242: 
243:           ret = parse_partition(&state, handler, arg);
244:         }
245:     }
246: 
247:   close_blockdriver(state.blk);
248:   return ret;
249: }

272:   struct mtd_geometry_s mgeo;

274: 
275:   ret = mtd->ioctl(mtd, MTDIOC_GEOMETRY, (unsigned long)(uintptr_t)&mgeo);
276:   if (ret < 0)
277:     {
278:       return ret;
279:     }
280: 
281:   DEBUGASSERT(mgeo.blocksize);
282: 
283:   state.blk       = NULL;
284:   state.mtd       = mtd;
285:   state.blocksize = mgeo.blocksize;
286:   state.erasesize = mgeo.erasesize;
287:   state.nblocks   = mgeo.neraseblocks;
288:   state.nblocks  *= mgeo.erasesize / mgeo.blocksize;
289: 
290:   return parse_partition(&state, handler, arg);

2. **High, blocking: the single-block CMD24 restriction is not enforced by Kconfig.**  
   The host rejects every write except exactly one 512-byte block at [bk7258_sdio.c:652](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:652), but `BK7258_SDIO` has no contract requiring `MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1` at [Kconfig:36](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/Kconfig:36). With the MMCSD default limit of zero, NuttX can enter its CMD25 path and submit a multi-block buffer at [mmcsd_sdio.c:2183](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:2183). That caller ignores the PIO `SDIO_SENDSETUP` return, so the host’s immediate `-EINVAL` becomes an event-wait timeout.

   Both modified defconfigs happen to set the limit to one, but any other valid configuration can enable a nonfunctional write path. The host option needs to require the limit, or the host must implement multi-block writes.

**Rechecked Areas**

The CMD24 FIFO/status implementation now matches the vendor register semantics: TX readiness comes from FIFO bit 19, completion uses write-end, and card acceptance uses interrupt-status bits 20–22. The unsigned FIFO timeout loops now test zero before decrementing at [bk7258_sdio.c:211](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:211) and [bk7258_sdio.c:751](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:751). The status accessor now snapshots mount state and source under `g_mmcsd_lock` at [bk7258_mmcsd.c:424](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:424); I found no remaining blocking accessor race.

**Verdict**

**Yes, blocking findings remain:** destructive provisioning does not safely quarantine stale partitions, and two valid Kconfig combinations expose unsupported or misleading behavior. No files were edited, and no hardware test or rebuild was performed.
